question.text: Suresh bought shares of ABC Ltd at INR 500 each. The stock has fallen to INR 320, but he refuses to sell, saying "I'll sell when it comes back to my purchase price." Meanwhile, he sold shares of XYZ Ltd at INR 180 which he bought at INR 150, booking a small profit. This pattern is known as the:

explanation.text: The Logic: Shefrin and Statman proposed the Disposition Effect to describe the tendency to hold losers too long and sell winners too early. The workbook reiterates that this bias explains holding losers longer and selling winners faster. Suresh refuses to sell ABC (loser) and books a small profit on XYZ (winner) — a textbook disposition pattern. The Trap: Anchoring Bias might seem relevant because Suresh anchors to his INR 500 purchase price, but the full pattern — holding losers while selling winners — is specifically the Disposition Effect. Endowment Effect is about overvaluing what you already own, not about the sell/hold asymmetry between winners and losers. Note: The Disposition Effect is rooted in loss aversion: realising a loss is psychologically painful, while realising a gain provides immediate satisfaction.
